info.name: Xolvon Backend — Complete API Collection
info.description:
# Xolvon Backend API — Postman Collection (plan T11)

Canonical contract: `docs/openapi.json` (59 paths / 65 operations, every one covered below) and
`docs/api-contract.md`. This collection supersedes the stray root
`Xolvon-API.postman_collection.json` (out-of-band commit `9a6d1d7`, non-conforming per DL-026);
all of its useful requests are ported here with test scripts, success + error examples, and
id/token capture. Relocation is recorded in DL-029 (`docs/decision-log.md`).

## Auth model: Bearer JWT only — the cookie jar is unused ON PURPOSE
The API is Bearer-only (DL-016/DL-018): it NEVER sets session cookies, so Postman's cookie jar
plays no role and no `Cookie` header is sent. Tokens are captured by TEST SCRIPTS into collection
variables (this replaces the "cookie flow" pattern a cookie-based API would use):

1. `01. Auth → Register user` creates the user (201, role is always `user` server-side).
2. `01. Auth → Login (user)` saves `accessToken` + `refreshToken` — collection variables.
3. Protected requests inherit collection-level `Bearer {{accessToken}}` auth.
4. `01. Auth → Login (admin)` saves `adminAccessToken`; every admin request overrides auth
   per-request to send `Bearer {{adminAccessToken}}` (so the user token stays valid for 06/07).
5. `Refresh access token` re-mints `accessToken` from `{{refreshToken}}`.
6. `Logout` revokes the refresh session — run it LAST in folder 01.

Token captures are LAYER-AWARE: if the selected environment defines the token variables (blank by
default), captures write to the environment layer because environment values shadow collection
variables in Postman resolution; without an active environment they write collection variables.

## Before a full (non-smoke) run
- Set the environment: `baseUrl`, `email`/`password`, `adminEmail`/`adminPassword`.
- Seed an admin first: `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL=... ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD=... npm run seed:admin`
  (never commit those values — DL-024).
- Folder order 01→09 doubles as a chain: creates capture ids (courseId, lessonId, orderId, ...) and
  later requests consume them, so a sequential pass against a fresh server builds its own data.

## Newman
    npm run test:newman   # full collection (needs seeded server)
    npx newman run postman/xolvon-backend.postman_collection.json \
      -e postman/environments/local.postman_environment.json --folder "10. Newman Smoke"

Folder `10. Newman Smoke` is self-contained (dynamic user, public + auth-chain only) and must pass
against a freshly migrated, EMPTY local server: `DB_DRIVER=sqlite STORAGE_DRIVER=local-test`.

## Request integrity (DL-018)
Mutations (POST/PATCH/DELETE) WITHOUT an Origin/Referer header pass the guard (service-to-service
clients like Postman/Newman). If you add an `Origin` header yourself, it must match an allowed
frontend origin (`CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`/`FRONTEND_URL`) or the server answers 403
`Request metadata is not allowed.` GETs are unaffected.

## Security
No real tokens, passwords, or keys in this file (DL-024). Bodies use class-validator-legal
placeholders only (example.com URLs, syntactically-valid phones, UUIDv4 placeholders).
